task: Your manager asks about last month's sign-ups. Answer with the numbers and the main reason. Sign-ups: September 5,000 → October 5,300. Main driver: the new referral campaign.
say: So how did sign-ups go last month?
zh: 经理问上个月的注册情况。用数据和主要原因回答。注册数：9月 5,000 → 10月 5,300。主要驱动因素：新的推荐活动。对方说：上个月注册情况怎么样？
example: They went well, thanks. We had 5,300 sign-ups in October, up 6 per cent on September. That was mainly driven by the new referral campaign.

task: Your manager is surprised revenue is flat. Explain using "offset by". New customers added +$120,000 a month; churn lost −$110,000 a month.
say: Why is revenue flat this month? I thought we'd signed lots of new customers.
zh: 经理对收入持平感到意外。用 "offset by" 来解释。新客户每月带来 +$120,000；客户流失每月损失 −$110,000。对方说：为什么这个月收入没变？我以为我们签了很多新客户。
example: We did. New customers added about 120,000 dollars. But that was almost completely offset by churn, which cost us around 110,000. So overall, we're only up about 10,000.

task: A colleague is excited about a survey result. Give a polite caveat about the sample size. Survey on the new feature: 14 of 18 respondents (78%) said they love it.
say: So 78% of customers love the new feature? That's great!
zh: 同事对一个调查结果很兴奋。礼貌地提醒样本量的问题。新功能调查：18 位回复者中有 14 人（78%）说很喜欢。对方说：78% 的客户都喜欢这个新功能？太棒了！
example: It's encouraging, but I'd be a bit careful. That's 14 out of only 18 people who answered, so it's a very small sample. I'd like to survey a bigger group before we draw any conclusions.

task: Your manager asks if the new pricing has worked. Say it's too early to tell. New pricing launched 10 days ago. Conversion: before 2.8% → since launch 3.1%.
say: Has the new pricing worked?
zh: 经理问新定价有没有效果。说现在下结论还太早。新定价 10 天前上线。转化率：之前 2.8% → 上线后 3.1%。对方说：新定价起作用了吗？
example: It's a bit too early to say. It's only been ten days. Conversion is up from 2.8 to 3.1 per cent, which looks promising, but I'd want at least a full month of data before we call it.

task: Your manager jumps to a conclusion. Explain politely that this is correlation, not causation, and suggest a way to test it. Users who turn on dark mode stay 20% longer than other users.
say: So if we make dark mode the default, retention will go up 20%, right?
zh: 经理太快下结论了。礼貌地解释这是相关性而不是因果关系，并建议一个验证方法。开启深色模式的用户比其他用户留存时间长 20%。对方说：那如果我们把深色模式设为默认，留存率就会提高 20%，对吧？
example: Not necessarily. People who turn on dark mode do stay about 20 per cent longer, but that's a correlation. They're probably keen power users to begin with. If we want to know for sure, we could run an A/B test.

task: Recommend a next step. Drop-off at the payment step: mobile 72%, desktop 45%.
say: What do you think we should do about the checkout drop-off?
zh: 推荐下一步行动。付款环节流失率：手机端 72%，电脑端 45%。对方说：你觉得结账流失的问题我们该怎么办？
example: I'd focus on mobile first. We lose 72 per cent of mobile users at the payment step, compared with 45 per cent on desktop. My suggestion is to review the mobile payment form and run a quick usability test next week.

task: Your manager asks for a breakdown you don't have. Admit it and offer to follow up. Total customer growth: +15%. Your report does not split it by country.
say: Do you know how much of that growth came from Australian customers?
zh: 经理问了一个你手头没有的细分数据。坦率承认并说明你会跟进。客户总增长：+15%。你的报告没有按国家细分。对方说：你知道这些增长里有多少来自澳大利亚客户吗？
example: Good question. I don't have that breakdown with me right now, but I can pull it from the data warehouse. I'll send it to you by the end of the day.

task: Sum up the quarter in one sentence. Q3: revenue +5%, costs −8%. It was the most profitable quarter this year.
say: If you had to sum it up in one sentence?
zh: 用一句话总结这个季度。第三季度：收入 +5%，成本 −8%。这是今年利润最高的一个季度。对方说：如果让你用一句话总结呢？
example: We grew revenue 5 per cent while cutting costs 8 per cent, so Q3 was our most profitable quarter this year.

task: Your manager thinks your numbers are wrong. Explain the difference politely. Last month's 3% churn was consumer customers only. This report includes business customers too: overall churn 4.5%.
say: These numbers look wrong. Last month you said churn was 3%.
zh: 经理觉得你的数据有问题。礼貌地解释差异。上个月的 3% 流失率只算了个人客户。这份报告也包括企业客户：总体流失率 4.5%。对方说：这些数字好像不对。上个月你说流失率是 3%。
example: I understand the confusion. Last month's 3 per cent was consumer customers only. This report includes business customers as well, which brings the overall rate to 4.5 per cent. I should've made that clearer on the slide.

task: Explain the jump in support tickets using "driven by". Tickets: September 2,000 → October 2,600. About 400 of the 600 extra tickets were about a bug in the iOS update.
say: Why did tickets jump so much in October?
zh: 用 "driven by" 解释支持工单的激增。工单：9月 2,000 → 10月 2,600。多出来的 600 张里约 400 张跟 iOS 更新的一个 bug 有关。对方说：为什么 10月工单涨了这么多？
example: Tickets went up 30 per cent, from 2,000 to 2,600. That was mostly driven by the bug in the iOS update. It accounts for about 400 of the 600 extra tickets.

task: A colleague thinks marketing caused the sales jump. Point out the seasonal pattern. Sales December vs November: this year +25%, last year +22%.
say: Sales jumped 25% in December compared with November. Is that our new marketing?
zh: 同事认为销售额大涨是营销的功劳。指出季节性规律。12月与11月相比的销售额：今年 +25%，去年 +22%。对方说：12月销售额比 11月涨了 25%，是我们新营销的效果吗？
example: It might be part of it, but December is always our busiest month because of Christmas. Last year, December was up 22 per cent on November, so most of this jump is probably seasonal.

task: Explain that one big deal is distorting the average. Average deal size: last quarter $12,000 → this quarter $19,000 (30 deals). One deal was $250,000. Without it, the average is about $11,000.
say: Average deal size is up almost 60%! What happened?
zh: 解释一笔大单扭曲了平均值。平均单笔金额：上季度 $12,000 → 本季度 $19,000（共 30 单）。其中一单是 $250,000。去掉这一单，平均约 $11,000。对方说：平均单笔金额涨了将近 60%！发生了什么？
example: It's mostly one deal, I'm afraid. We closed a single $250,000 contract, which pulls the average up a lot. If we take that one out, the average is about $11,000, which is actually a little down on last quarter.

task: Explain that the drop is a data problem, not a real drop. Website traffic in September: −40%. The tracking code was missing for 5 days after a release. It is fixed, and October looks normal.
say: Traffic dropped 40% in September. Should we be worried?
zh: 解释这次下降是数据问题，不是真实的下降。9月网站流量：−40%。一次发布后跟踪代码丢失了 5 天。已经修复，10月数据正常。对方说：9月流量下降了 40%。我们需要担心吗？
example: I don't think so. The tracking code was missing from the site for five days after the release, so that drop is mostly a data issue, not real lost traffic. We've fixed it, and October looks normal again.

task: Recommend a quick way to cut the cloud bill. Cloud costs: $46,000 a month. Budget: $40,000. Idle development servers that nobody uses cost about $5,000 a month.
say: What can we do about the cloud bill?
zh: 推荐一个快速降低云账单的办法。云成本：每月 $46,000。预算：$40,000。没人用的闲置开发服务器每月约 $5,000。对方说：云账单我们能做点什么？
example: The quickest win is the idle development servers. They're costing us about $5,000 a month and nobody's using them. If we switch them off, we'd be at around $41,000, so close to budget again.

task: Your manager asks why one store did badly. Give a possible reason, say it's not confirmed, and promise a follow-up. Christchurch store sales: −18%. Possible reason: roadworks outside since August (not confirmed).
say: Why did the Christchurch store do so badly?
zh: 经理问为什么某家店业绩很差。给出一个可能的原因，说明还没有证实，并承诺跟进。基督城门店销售额：−18%。可能原因：8月以来门口在修路（未证实）。对方说：基督城那家店为什么表现这么差？
example: I'm not a hundred per cent sure yet. Sales there were down 18 per cent, and one possible reason is the roadworks outside since August. But I haven't confirmed that, so I'll check the foot traffic data and come back to you on Thursday.

task: Give a short summary for the executive team. Last quarter: uptime 99.98%, zero priority-one (P1) incidents.
say: Quick summary for the exec team?
zh: 给管理层一个简短的总结。上季度：正常运行时间 99.98%，零个一级（P1）事故。对方说：能给管理层来个简短总结吗？
example: Short version: it was a very stable quarter. Uptime was 99.98 per cent, and we had zero priority-one incidents.

task: Your manager draws a conclusion too quickly. Give another explanation. Office-based teams deliver 12% more story points. But they are also the more senior teams.
say: So working from the office makes people more productive?
zh: 经理太快下结论了。给出另一种解释。坐班的团队多完成 12% 的故事点。但他们也是资历更深的团队。对方说：所以在办公室上班会让人更有效率？
example: Not necessarily. The office-based teams do deliver about 12 per cent more, but they're also our more senior teams. So it could be experience rather than location. We'd need to compare similar teams to know for sure.

task: Your manager wants an unrealistic target. Push back politely with the numbers and offer an alternative. App users now: 30,000. Growth: about 3% a month. March is 4 months away. At this rate: about 34,000 by March.
say: Can we commit to doubling app users by March?
zh: 经理想定一个不现实的目标。用数据礼貌地反驳，并提出替代方案。现在的应用用户：30,000。增长：每月约 3%。离 3月还有 4 个月。按这个速度：3月约 34,000。对方说：我们能承诺到 3月把应用用户翻一番吗？
example: I'd be careful with that. We're growing about 3 per cent a month, so by March we'd expect around 34,000 users, not 60,000. Doubling would need a big new channel. Maybe we could agree on a stretch target of 40,000 instead?

task: A colleague asks about the new chatbot. Give the key number. First month: the chatbot resolved 35% of chats without a human.
say: How's the new chatbot doing?
zh: 同事问新聊天机器人的情况。给出关键数据。第一个月：聊天机器人在没有人工参与的情况下解决了 35% 的对话。对方说：新的聊天机器人表现怎么样？
example: It's going well. In its first month, the chatbot resolved 35 per cent of chats without a human getting involved.

task: Explain why total costs barely fell, using "offset by". Hardware spending: −$30,000. Software licence price increase: +$25,000.
say: We cut hardware spending, so why haven't total costs gone down much?
zh: 用 "offset by" 解释为什么总成本几乎没降。硬件支出：−$30,000。软件许可证涨价：+$25,000。对方说：我们削减了硬件支出，为什么总成本没怎么降？
example: We did save about 30,000 dollars on hardware, but most of that was offset by the licence price increase, which added 25,000. So the net saving is only around 5,000.

task: Explain the drop in logged hours. Project hours: September 3,400 → October 3,100. October had Labour Day and the school holidays, so many people took leave. Hours per working day were about the same.
say: Why did the team log fewer hours in October?
zh: 解释登记工时的下降。项目工时：9月 3,400 → 10月 3,100。10月有劳动节和学校假期，很多人请了假。每个工作日的工时基本持平。对方说：为什么团队 10月登记的工时少了？
example: It's mainly the calendar. October had Labour Day and the school holidays, so a lot of people took leave. Hours dropped from 3,400 to 3,100, but per working day we're about the same as September.

task: Your manager wants to roll out a test winner too early. Explain that the result isn't significant and suggest what to do. A/B test: version A 3.2%, version B 3.3%, 2,000 users in each group. Not statistically significant.
say: Version B won, so let's roll it out.
zh: 经理想过早上线测试中的胜出版本。解释结果并不显著，并建议怎么做。A/B 测试：A 版 3.2%，B 版 3.3%，每组 2,000 名用户。在统计上不显著。对方说：B 版赢了，那就上线吧。
example: I'd hold off for now. B is only slightly ahead, 3.3 versus 3.2 per cent, and with just 2,000 users in each group, that difference isn't statistically significant. It could easily be noise. I'd suggest running the test for another two weeks.

task: Correct a mistake in last week's report. You wrote October revenue was $1.32M. It should be $1.23M. You have sent an updated version.
say: Before we start, is there anything to flag?
zh: 更正上周报告中的一个错误。你写的 10月收入是 $1.32M，应该是 $1.23M。你已经发了更新版本。对方说：开始之前，有什么需要提一下的吗？
example: Yes, one correction. In last week's report, I said October revenue was 1.32 million. It should've been 1.23 million. I swapped two digits. Sorry about that, and I've sent out an updated version.

task: Recommend reducing the van fleet over winter. Vans leased: 80. July: 49 in use on average (61%), never more than 62 on any day.
say: Do we really need all 80 vans?
zh: 建议冬季减少货车数量。租赁货车：80 辆。7月：平均使用 49 辆（61%），任何一天都没超过 62 辆。对方说：我们真的需要全部 80 辆货车吗？
example: Probably not over winter. In July we used 49 vans on average, about 61 per cent, and never more than 62. If we returned ten vans for the winter months, we'd still have a buffer of eight on our busiest day.

task: Explain what is behind the rise in NPS. NPS: 28 → 36. Average first response time: 8 hours → 2 hours. Many positive comments mention speed.
say: What's behind the jump in NPS?
zh: 解释 NPS 上升的原因。NPS：28 → 36。平均首次响应时间：8 小时 → 2 小时。很多正面评论都提到了速度。对方说：NPS 大涨的原因是什么？
example: The main driver seems to be faster support. Our first response time dropped from eight hours to two, and a lot of the positive comments mention speed. That helped push NPS up eight points, from 28 to 36.

task: Your manager wants to publish a survey score. Give a caveat about the low response rate. Customer satisfaction: 8.9/10. Response rate: 6%.
say: Customers rate us 8.9 out of 10. Can we put that in the annual report?
zh: 经理想公开一个调查分数。就回复率低给出提醒。客户满意度：8.9/10。回复率：6%。对方说：客户给我们打了 8.9 分（满分 10 分）。可以写进年报吗？
example: I'd be a bit careful. Only 6 per cent of customers responded, and happy customers are often the ones who reply. So 8.9 is probably on the high side. If we use it, we should mention the response rate.

task: Give a quick uptime update. Uptime last month: 99.95%. Target: 99.9%.
say: Any update on server uptime?
zh: 简单汇报一下正常运行时间。上月正常运行时间：99.95%。目标：99.9%。对方说：服务器正常运行时间有什么新情况吗？
example: Yes, all good. Uptime last month was 99.95 per cent, so we're comfortably above our 99.9 target.

task: Your manager asks for a number you haven't calculated. Admit it and offer a time to follow up. You have support and hosting data, but haven't split costs by customer type.
say: What's the cost to serve an enterprise customer versus a small business?
zh: 经理问了一个你还没算过的数字。坦率承认，并给出跟进时间。你有支持和托管的数据，但还没有按客户类型拆分成本。对方说：服务一个企业客户和一个小企业客户的成本分别是多少？
example: That's a great question, and honestly, I haven't broken it down that way yet. I can work it out from the support and hosting data. Can I get back to you by Friday?

task: The CFO challenges your forecast. Accept the point, explain what went wrong and what you changed. Last quarter: forecast $2.0M, actual $1.7M (−15%), because one large contract was delayed. The new model weights deals by probability and shows a range.
say: Your forecast was off by 15% last quarter. Why should we trust this one?
zh: CFO 质疑你的预测。接受批评，解释哪里出了问题以及你做了哪些改进。上季度：预测 $2.0M，实际 $1.7M（−15%），原因是一份大合同推迟了。新模型按成交概率给交易加权，并给出一个区间。对方说：上季度你的预测差了 15%。我们为什么要相信这次的？
example: That's fair. Last quarter we forecast 2 million and came in at 1.7, mainly because one large contract slipped. Since then, we've changed the model. We now weight deals by probability and show a range, not a single number. I'm happy to walk you through the assumptions.

task: A colleague wants to drop the free trial. Disagree politely with the numbers and suggest a test. Trial users convert at 8%. Visitors who don't trial convert at 2%.
say: Should we drop the free trial? Trial users don't convert much.
zh: 同事想取消免费试用。用数据礼貌地表示不同意，并建议做个测试。试用用户转化率 8%。不试用的访客转化率 2%。对方说：我们要不要取消免费试用？试用用户转化得不多。
example: I wouldn't drop it yet. Trial users actually convert at 8 per cent, compared with 2 per cent for visitors who don't trial, so that's four times better. If anything, I'd test a shorter trial first and see what happens.

task: Your manager is worried about sales part-way through the month. Explain why it's too soon to worry. November sales so far (10 days): $310,000. Target: $1M. Last year, 70% of November sales came in the last two weeks (Black Friday).
say: We're way behind on November sales, aren't we?
zh: 经理在月中担心销售情况。解释为什么现在担心还太早。11月至今（10 天）销售额：$310,000。目标：$1M。去年 11月 70% 的销售额来自最后两周（黑色星期五）。对方说：11月的销售远远落后了，是不是？
example: Not necessarily. We're at 310,000 after ten days, which looks low against a million-dollar target. But last year, 70 per cent of November sales came in the last two weeks, around Black Friday. So I'd wait until the end of the month.

task: Explain a mix effect. Average revenue per user (ARPU): −5%. Prices did not change. ARPU went up in every customer segment. Most new customers joined the cheaper small business plan.
say: ARPU fell 5%. Are we charging less?
zh: 解释结构（组合）效应。每用户平均收入（ARPU）：−5%。价格没有变。每个客户细分的 ARPU 都上升了。大多数新客户选的是更便宜的小企业套餐。对方说：ARPU 下降了 5%。我们收费变少了吗？
example: No, prices haven't changed. Revenue per user actually went up in every segment. The overall average fell because most of our new customers are on the small business plan, which is cheaper. So it's a mix effect, not a pricing problem.

task: Your manager asks if the LED upgrade worked. Answer, with a caveat about the weather. Energy use since the upgrade: −12%. This winter was milder than usual. Facilities estimate the LEDs explain about half of the saving.
say: Did the LED upgrade cut our power bill?
zh: 经理问 LED 升级有没有效果。回答，并就天气因素给出提醒。升级以来用电量：−12%。今年冬天比往年暖和。后勤部门估计大约一半的节省来自 LED。对方说：LED 升级降低我们的电费了吗？
example: It looks like it helped. Energy use is down 12 per cent since the upgrade. But this winter was also milder than usual, so part of that is the weather. Facilities reckon the LEDs explain about half of the saving.

task: Your manager asks about the biggest risk. Answer and recommend an action. Our three biggest customers make up 70% of revenue.
say: What's the biggest risk you see in these numbers?
zh: 经理问最大的风险是什么。回答并建议一个行动。我们最大的三个客户占收入的 70%。对方说：你从这些数字里看到的最大风险是什么？
example: For me, it's concentration. Our three biggest customers make up 70 per cent of revenue, so if even one of them left, we'd lose a big chunk of income. I'd recommend we focus on growing our mid-sized accounts.

task: Your manager understated the result. Politely correct them, using percentage points. Conversion rate: 3% → 5%.
say: So conversion only went up 2%?
zh: 经理把结果说小了。用百分点礼貌地纠正。转化率：3% → 5%。对方说：所以转化率只涨了 2%？
example: Actually, it's a bit better than that. It went from 3 to 5 per cent, so that's up two percentage points. In relative terms, it's about a 67 per cent increase.

task: Explain the uptime dip and what you did about it. August uptime: 99.6%. Cause: a failed storage upgrade caused a 3-hour outage. The root cause is fixed, and a rollback step has been added.
say: Why did uptime drop in August?
zh: 解释正常运行时间下降的原因以及采取的措施。8月正常运行时间：99.6%。原因：一次存储升级失败，导致 3 小时停机。根本原因已修复，并增加了回滚步骤。对方说：8月正常运行时间为什么下降了？
example: It was mainly one incident. A storage upgrade failed and we had a three-hour outage, which on its own took us down to 99.6 per cent for the month. We've fixed the root cause and added a rollback step to the upgrade process.

task: A colleague reads the data the wrong way round. Disagree politely and suggest a better analysis. Customers who call support are more likely to cancel.
say: Customers who call support churn more, so support is making them leave.
zh: 同事把数据的因果关系看反了。礼貌地表示不同意，并建议更好的分析方法。打过客服电话的客户更有可能取消。对方说：打客服电话的客户流失得更多，所以是客服把他们赶走了。
example: I see why it looks that way, but I think it's the other way round. People usually call support because something's already gone wrong, and that problem drives both the call and the cancellation. I'd look at what they're calling about.

task: Give the main takeaway from the staff survey. 81% would recommend us as a place to work, up from 74% last year.
say: So what's the main takeaway from the survey?
zh: 说出员工调查的主要结论。81% 的人会推荐我们公司作为工作单位，去年是 74%。对方说：这次调查的主要结论是什么？
example: The main takeaway is that people are happier at work. 81 per cent would recommend us as a place to work, up from 74 per cent last year.

task: Recommend an action from the ticket data and estimate the effect. Password resets are 35% of all support tickets.
say: So what should we do with this?
zh: 根据工单数据推荐一个行动，并估算效果。密码重置占所有支持工单的 35%。对方说：那我们该怎么利用这些数据？
example: I'd suggest a self-service password reset. Resets are 35 per cent of our tickets, so even if we only cut half of them, that's more than 17 per cent fewer tickets overall. That would free up a lot of the team's time.

task: Your manager wants one number. Give the best estimate but mention the range. Q1 revenue forecast: $3.4M. Likely range: $3.1M–$3.7M, depending on two big renewals.
say: Just give me one number for Q1.
zh: 经理只想要一个数字。给出最佳估计，但提一下区间。第一季度收入预测：$3.4M。可能区间：$3.1M–$3.7M，取决于两份大的续约。对方说：给我一个第一季度的数字就行。
example: Our best estimate is 3.4 million, so if you need one number, that's it. But it could reasonably be anywhere between 3.1 and 3.7, depending on whether the two big renewals come through.

task: Explain how you calculated churn, with an example. Churn = customers who cancelled during the month ÷ customers at the start of the month. October: 90 cancelled out of 3,000.
say: How did you calculate churn?
zh: 解释你是怎么计算流失率的，并举例。流失率 = 当月取消的客户数 ÷ 月初客户数。10月：3,000 个客户中有 90 个取消。对方说：流失率你是怎么算的？
example: We take the number of customers who cancelled during the month and divide it by the number we had at the start. So in October, 90 out of 3,000 cancelled, which gives us 3 per cent.

task: A colleague wants to stop LinkedIn ads. Disagree politely with the numbers. LinkedIn brings 8% of leads but 30% of closed deals.
say: Let's stop spending on LinkedIn ads. They bring in hardly any leads.
zh: 同事想停掉 LinkedIn 广告。用数据礼貌地表示不同意。LinkedIn 带来 8% 的潜在客户，但贡献了 30% 的成交。对方说：我们停掉 LinkedIn 广告吧，它几乎带不来什么潜在客户。
example: I'd be careful with that. LinkedIn only brings in 8 per cent of our leads, but those leads turn into 30 per cent of our closed deals. They're much higher quality, so cutting it could actually hurt sales.

task: Give bad news about a project clearly and calmly. Migration project: 3 weeks behind schedule. Forecast cost $230,000 vs budget $200,000. Main cause: legacy data messier than expected. You have a recovery plan.
say: Where are we on the migration project?
zh: 清楚、冷静地报告项目的坏消息。迁移项目：落后计划 3 周。预计成本 $230,000，预算 $200,000。主要原因：旧数据比预期更乱。你有一个补救计划。对方说：迁移项目进展到哪儿了？
example: I'm afraid it's not great news. We're about three weeks behind, and we're forecasting 230,000 dollars against a budget of 200,000, so 15 per cent over. The main cause is that the legacy data is messier than expected. I've got a recovery plan I'd like to walk you through.

task: Your manager asks if a number is good or bad. Answer with context. Average ticket resolution time: 5.2 hours. Our target: 6 hours. Industry benchmark: about 8 hours.
say: Is that number good or bad?
zh: 经理问这个数字是好还是坏。结合背景回答。平均工单解决时间：5.2 小时。我们的目标：6 小时。行业基准：约 8 小时。对方说：这个数字算好还是不好？
example: It's good. Our average resolution time is 5.2 hours, which beats our own target of six and the industry benchmark of about eight.

task: Your manager asks something your data can't answer. Explain the limit, give what you do know, and offer a fix. We track opens and clicks for each email, not purchases. Highest click rate: the October sale email, 6%.
say: Can you tell which marketing email drove the most sales?
zh: 经理问了一个你的数据回答不了的问题。说明数据的局限，给出你知道的信息，并提出改进办法。我们跟踪每封邮件的打开和点击，但不跟踪购买。点击率最高：10月促销邮件，6%。对方说：你能看出哪封营销邮件带来的销售最多吗？
example: Not exactly, unfortunately. We track opens and clicks for each email, but we don't link them to purchases yet. The October sale email had the highest click rate, at 6 per cent. I can set up purchase tracking so we can answer this properly next time.

task: A colleague is impressed by a big percentage. Explain the small-base effect. Hamilton sales: $40,000 → $60,000 (+50%). Auckland sales: $2.0M → $2.2M (+10%).
say: Hamilton grew 50%! Should we copy what they're doing everywhere?
zh: 同事被一个很大的百分比打动了。解释基数小的影响。汉密尔顿销售额：$40,000 → $60,000（+50%）。奥克兰销售额：$2.0M → $2.2M（+10%）。对方说：汉密尔顿增长了 50%！我们要不要在所有地方都照搬他们的做法？
example: It's a great result, but the base is small. Hamilton went from 40,000 to 60,000, so that's an extra 20,000. Auckland only grew 10 per cent, but that's an extra 200,000, ten times as much in dollars. Worth a look, but let's not over-read the percentage.

task: A senior manager says your survey sample is biased. Agree, explain the effect and say how you'll fix it. You surveyed only customers who logged in this month.
say: Isn't your sample biased? You only surveyed customers who logged in this month.
zh: 一位高层经理说你的调查样本有偏差。表示同意，解释影响，并说明你会怎么改进。你只调查了本月登录过的客户。对方说：你的样本不是有偏差吗？你只调查了这个月登录过的客户。
example: Yes, that's a fair point. Because we only surveyed active users, we've missed people who've stopped using the product, and they're probably the least happy. I'll add a note to the slide, and next time we'll include customers who haven't logged in recently.

task: Give the headline and a recommendation. Year on year: revenue +9%, costs +14%. Profit margin: 25% → about 22%.
say: Give me the headline.
zh: 给出核心结论和一个建议。同比：收入 +9%，成本 +14%。利润率：25% → 约 22%。对方说：给我说说重点。
example: The headline is that costs are growing faster than revenue. Revenue is up 9 per cent year on year, but costs are up 14, so our margin has slipped from 25 to about 22 per cent. We should review costs before the next budget round.

task: Your manager asks when you'll reach a milestone. Give an estimate with an assumption and a caveat. Users now: 82,000. Adding about 3,000 a month. It is November. Summer holidays usually slow growth.
say: When will we hit 100,000 users?
zh: 经理问什么时候能达到一个里程碑。给出估计，说明假设并提醒风险。现在的用户：82,000。每月新增约 3,000。现在是 11月。夏季假期通常会让增长放缓。对方说：我们什么时候能达到 10 万用户？
example: If we keep adding about 3,000 users a month, we'll hit 100,000 in six months, so around May. But that assumes growth stays steady, and the summer holidays usually slow things down.

task: Your manager wants a straight answer on whether a project was worth it. Answer, give the payback period and one caveat. Project cost: $180,000. Savings: about $120,000 a year, based on the first four months.
say: Just tell me straight: was the project worth it?
zh: 经理想要一个直接的回答：这个项目值不值。回答，给出回本周期和一个提醒。项目成本：$180,000。节省：每年约 $120,000（基于前四个月的数据）。对方说：直接告诉我，这个项目值不值得？
example: Yes, I think it was. It cost 180,000 dollars, and it's saving us about 120,000 a year, so it pays for itself in a year and a half. The only caveat is that the savings are based on the first four months, so we'll confirm it at year end.
